evidence: Directly inspected the actual frozen XLSX using openpyxl: Quality Checks row 3 identifies check 2 and requires an authentic human voice; Internal Quality Checks row 3 repeats it without an additional annotation. Deterministic Checks row 13 explicitly leaves voice and grammar to the rubric, so no keyword or word-count script was treated as a voice verdict. Applied the frozen skill's references/quality-checks.md:13-15 (sentence variety, contractions, terse fragments; beware uniform cadence, marketing gloss and changes of voice). Read instruction.md and all six shipped /instructions files in full, and checked environment/Dockerfile's COPY instructions/ /instructions/ to establish the builder-facing set. The main request has a personal motive, contractions and varied sentence lengths: task/instruction.md:1, 'I'd like a small code playground' and 'No accounts or sign-in; it's a local tool'; :3, 'The annoying part with playgrounds is losing something that was working'; :7, 'I also need to start a fresh draft'. Every note sustains direct, ordinary language despite different technical subjects: environment/instructions/overview.md:3 says 'When I open the app, I want useful code already there' and :5 'I shouldn't have to keep a separate selector in sync'; behaviour.md:11 gives a concrete human situation, 'I might leave it there for a while before clicking a button or typing into a field', while :13 says 'I don't want half of the failed attempt left behind' and :21 uses the short sentence 'About two seconds after I stop typing is plenty'; ui.md:3 starts 'I'd like the editor, preview and console visible as three useful panes' and :7 leaves control wording and placement to the builder; policy.md:3 uses 'There's no account data or authentication to build' and :5 gives a plain list of choices without marketing language; integration.md:3 says the tools 'would be convenient' but 'are up to you', and :7/:11 use 'shouldn't' and 'mustn't' naturally alongside exact runtime facts; security.md:5 begins 'Please support ordinary source-written JavaScript' and :7 contrasts prohibited execution with harmless words in strings, comments or HTML text in straightforward prose. The technical notes are more detailed than the opening request but retain its plain, personal voice; factual precision alone does not establish a robotic register. There are no perfectly parallel bullet lists in these seven documents, and their mixture of short instructions, longer explanations and concrete situations does not have uniform cadence. The seed's short explanatory note is similarly plain. The staged contract permits operating notes and requires runtime precision; the frozen template integration note supplies the same kind of Node/SQLite/runtime detail, so treating those nouns and paths as a voice defect would be a false positive. No credible defect was identified. This is a source-style assessment, not a claim about who authored the prose. No browser/model run is necessary to establish this row, and no full-judge timing, Oracle result or target-model score is inferred.
counterexample: Applied two explicit source-review stress cases, without modifying the frozen task. A conforming terse technical note such as 'Start it with node /app/server.js. Keep saved snippets after a restart.' would lack first-person wording or contractions but still be natural human prose; that prevents falsely failing integration.md:5 solely for imperative runtime instructions. Conversely, replacing each note's paragraph with repeated 'The application shall seamlessly provide a robust ...' clauses would preserve product nouns, file paths and many mechanical content checks while creating the robotic/marketing cadence this row rejects. Reading the complete seven-file instruction set distinguishes that plausible false pass; the frozen text instead contains the varied, concrete passages cited above. These are prose counterexamples, not executed application mutations, because application behavior does not determine the voice of the supplied request.
